90-90-switch.description: A hip-mobility drill in which you sit with both knees bent at right angles and rotate your legs from one side to the other, keeping the 90/90 position on each side. It trains the internal and external rotation of both hips as you switch.
instructions: Sit on the floor with the front knee bent at 90 degrees and the back knee bent at 90 degrees, and place your hands behind you for support.
Sit tall and keep your trunk upright.
Lift both knees slightly and rotate your legs to the other side in a controlled movement, so that the front leg becomes the back leg.
Settle into the 90/90 position on the new side, using your hands for balance.
Switch back to the first side, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
Keep the movement slow and smooth, without forcing the hips.
tips: Keep your trunk tall; leaning back too far takes the work out of the hips.
Do the 90/90 hold first if you cannot reach the position on both sides.
Move slowly and stop if you feel pinching in the hip or pain in the knee.

archer-push-ups.description: A wide push-up lowering toward one hand while the opposite arm stays straight, loading one side at a time.
instructions: Set up in a wide push-up position with arms straight.
Lower yourself toward one hand while keeping the other arm straight.
Keep your core tight and body in a straight line.
Press back up to the start position.
Alternate sides each rep for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your hips square to the floor as you shift sideways.
Let the straight arm assist as little as possible.
Start from wide push-ups and shift a little further each session.

back-extension.description: An isolation movement targeting the lower back erector spinae on a hyperextension bench.
instructions: Lie face down on a hyperextension bench with hips at the pad edge.
Lower your upper body toward the floor.
Raise your torso back up until your body is straight.
Repeat.
tips: Keep movements controlled.
Do not hyperextend beyond neutral spine.

balance-dome-plank.description: A forearm plank with the elbows on a balance dome. The unstable surface makes the shoulders and the whole trunk work harder to keep the body in a straight line from head to heels.
instructions: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and kneel behind it.
Put your forearms on the dome with your elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back into a plank with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abdominals, keeping your neck long.
Hold the position for the planned time while the dome moves under you.
Lower your knees to the floor to finish.
tips: Do not let your hips sag or pike up; a straight line from head to heels is the target.
Press your forearms into the dome and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Make it easier by widening your feet, or harder by bringing them closer together.

balance-dome-squat-hold.description: A static squat held on a balance dome: you stand on the domed top and lower into a partial squat with your arms reaching forward, then stay there while the unstable surface keeps shifting. The quadriceps and glutes hold the position and the ankles and trunk work to keep you balanced.
instructions: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and step onto the middle of it with both feet, about hip-width apart.
Stand tall and find your balance before you start to squat.
Push your hips back and bend your knees until your thighs are close to parallel with the floor.
Reach your arms straight out in front of you to counterbalance and keep your chest up.
Hold the position for the planned time, keeping your knees in line with your toes.
Stand up slowly and step off one foot at a time.
tips: Master the plain balance dome stand first; the squat adds load to an unstable surface.
Spread your weight across the whole foot and do not let your heels lift or your knees cave inward.
Hold a wall or a rack with one hand while you learn the position.

ball-pike.description: An advanced core exercise where the hips pike up while the feet roll a stability ball toward the chest.
instructions: Place the shins on a stability ball and hands on the floor in a high plank.
Brace the core and keep the legs straight.
Pike the hips up, rolling the ball toward the chest as the body forms an inverted V.
Pause briefly at the top.
Roll the ball back out to the starting plank.
tips: Keep the legs straight throughout — no knee bend.
Move at the hips, not the lower back.
Build up with knee tucks first if the pike is too hard.

banded-ankle-stretch.description: A seated stretch that uses a band around the forefoot to flex the ankle and lengthen the calf.
instructions: Sit with one leg extended and a band around the forefoot.
Hold the band in both hands.
Pull so the toes draw back toward your shin.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the leg straight and relaxed.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.

banded-figure-4-stretch.description: A lying glute stretch in a figure-4 position, using a band to draw both legs toward the chest.
instructions: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite thigh.
Loop a band around the supporting thigh.
Pull both legs toward your chest with the band.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Let the crossed knee fall open.

banded-hamstring-stretch.description: A lying stretch that uses a band around the foot to draw a straight leg toward the torso and lengthen the hamstring.
instructions: Lie on your back and loop a band around one foot.
Raise that leg straight up, holding the band in both hands.
Gently pull the band to draw the leg toward you.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the raised leg as straight as you can.
Keep the other leg flat on the floor.

banded-lat-stretch.description: A standing stretch that lengthens the lats by hinging forward while holding a band overhead under tension.
instructions: Hold a band overhead with both hands under light tension.
Hinge forward at the hips with your arms reaching ahead.
Let your chest sink to lengthen the sides of your back.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your arms straight and shoulders relaxed.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

banded-seated-hip-abduction.description: This isolation exercise targets the gluteus medius and maximus by externally rotating the hips against band resistance while seated.
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with a loop band around your knees.
Keep your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and maintain an upright posture.
Push your knees outwards against the band, engaging your glutes.
Hold the peak contraction briefly, then slowly return your knees to the starting position.
Control the movement throughout the entire range of motion.
tips: Focus on squeezing your glutes to initiate the movement.
Avoid leaning back or using momentum; keep your torso stable.
Choose a band resistance that allows for controlled movement.
Maintain tension on the band even in the starting position.

banded-standing-hip-abduction.description: This isolation exercise targets the gluteus medius and maximus, improving hip stability and strength by abducting the leg against band resistance.
instructions: Place a loop band around your ankles or just above your knees.
Stand tall with a slight bend in your knees and brace your core.
Shift your weight onto one leg, maintaining a stable torso.
Slowly abduct the free leg out to the side, feeling the glute contract.
Control the movement as you return the leg to the starting position.
Complete all reps per side before switching.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to the side.
Focus on a controlled movement, not momentum.
Ensure the band maintains tension throughout the entire range of motion.
Initiate the movement from your hip, not your foot.

banded-triceps-stretch.description: A standing stretch that lengthens the triceps by reaching one hand behind the head against band tension.
instructions: Hold a band that runs down your back, top hand behind your head.
Anchor the lower hand at your lower back.
Reach the top hand down to feel the triceps lengthen.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your head upright and ribs down.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

barbell-calf-raise.description: A standing calf raise loaded with a barbell across the upper back, using a raised platform for a deeper heel stretch.
instructions: Place a barbell across your upper back as in a squat.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised platform.
Push up onto your toes as high as possible.
Pause and squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower your heels below the platform and repeat.
tips: Avoid bouncing out of the bottom stretch position.
Keep your knees straight but not locked throughout the set.
Move slowly to stay balanced under the bar.

barbell-isometric-squat-hold.description: An isometric version of the barbell back squat: you squat down with the bar on your upper back and hold the bottom position. The quadriceps, glutes and the muscles that keep your back rigid stay under tension at the deepest, hardest point of the squat.
instructions: Set the bar on your upper back, grip it just outside your shoulders and step back from the rack with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Take a big breath into your belly, brace your core and keep your chest tall.
Sit down and back until your thighs are about parallel to the floor or a little below, with your knees tracking over your toes.
Stop at the bottom and hold the position, with your weight over the middle of your feet.
Keep your back flat and your knees pushed out while you hold for the planned time.
Drive up through your feet to stand, then rack the bar.
tips: Use safety arms or pins set just below your bottom position, since a long hold at depth is tiring.
Choose a lighter bar than your working squat weight; holding for time is harder than it looks.
Keep the knees pushed out over the toes instead of letting them collapse inward as you tire.

barbell-pullover.description: A compound movement stretching and loading the lats and chest through a wide arc.
instructions: Lie across a bench with a barbell held over your chest.
Lower the bar back over your head in an arc.
Pull it back to the start over your chest.
Repeat.
tips: Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
Engage the lats to drive the bar back.

barbell-wrist-curl.description: A barbell wrist curl that isolates the forearm flexors for grip and forearm size.
instructions: Sit on a bench with forearms resting on the thighs, palms up.
Hold a barbell with hands shoulder-width, wrists hanging off the knees.
Let the bar roll down to the fingertips at the bottom.
Curl the bar up by flexing the wrists.
Lower under control.
tips: Move only at the wrist — keep the forearms still.
Roll the bar to the fingertips for full range.
Use a thumbless grip if it helps wrist comfort.

battle-ropes.description: A high-intensity conditioning movement using thick ropes, training the upper back, shoulders, and grip.
instructions: Anchor the ropes to a fixed point and grab one end in each hand.
Step back so the ropes have moderate slack.
Drop into a quarter squat with feet shoulder-width.
Drive each arm up and down rapidly to send waves through the ropes.
Continue for the prescribed work interval.
tips: Stay in the quarter-squat the entire interval.
Drive force from the legs and hips, not just the arms.
Keep the waves consistent and tight.

behind-the-neck-lat-pulldown.description: A wide-grip lat pulldown taken behind the head, targeting the upper lats and traps — requires full overhead shoulder mobility.
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown station with thighs secured under the pad.
Grip the bar with a wide, overhand grip — wider than shoulder-width.
Keep the torso upright and tuck the chin slightly forward.
Pull the bar down behind the head until it touches the base of the neck.
Return under control to the full overhead stretch.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Only perform this if you have full, pain-free overhead shoulder mobility.
Use a moderate load — this is not a strength lift, it's a hypertrophy accessory.

bench-ankle-stretch.description: A standing stretch with the foot flat on a bench, driving the knee forward over the toes to flex the ankle.
instructions: Place one whole foot flat on top of a bench.
Keep your torso upright.
Drive that knee forward over your toes.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your heel down on the bench.
Move slowly and keep the foot flat.

bench-childs-pose.description: A kneeling stretch with the arms resting on a bench, sitting the hips back to lengthen the lats and lower back.
instructions: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench.
Extend both arms forward and rest them on the bench.
Sit your hips back toward your heels and let the chest sink.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your arms straight and relax your neck.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

bench-figure-4-glute-stretch.description: A seated stretch on a bench with one ankle crossed over the knee, hinging forward to target the glute.
instructions: Sit on the end of a bench.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Keep your back flat and hinge forward over the crossed leg.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Let the crossed knee fall open.
Hinge from the hips, keeping the chest open.

bench-leg-pull-in.description: A seated core exercise on a flat bench: leaning back with your hands on the bench, you pull the knees toward the chest to train the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Sit on a flat bench, grip its edges beside or just behind your hips and lean your torso back slightly.
Extend your legs out in front of you with your feet off the floor.
Pull your knees toward your chest, bringing the torso slightly forward to meet them.
Extend the legs back out under control without letting your feet touch the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest lifted and your back straight; do not round forward.
Control the eccentric; do not let gravity drop the legs.
Squeeze the abs at the top of each rep for a stronger contraction.

bent-arm-ez-bar-pullover.description: A bent-arm pullover on a flat bench using an EZ-bar — wrist-friendlier than the straight barbell version while keeping the deep lat and pec stretch.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ-bar with a narrow overhand grip on the inner bends.
Start with the bar above your chest, elbows bent to roughly 90 degrees.
Keep the elbow angle fixed and lower the bar back in an arc overhead until a deep stretch is felt in the lats and pecs.
Pull the bar back over the chest along the same arc, without straightening the elbows.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The elbow angle stays fixed — only the shoulder moves.
Bent elbows shorten the lever, so you can usually handle a little more weight than in a straight-arm pullover.
If the lower back arches, plant the feet more firmly and brace the abs.

bicep-curl.description: An isolation exercise targeting the biceps.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Avoid swinging the weights.

boat-pose.description: A seated balance on the sit bones with the legs lifted and the chest tall, holding a V shape that loads the hip flexors and the whole front of the trunk.
instructions: Sit on the floor with the knees bent and the feet flat, hands resting behind the thighs.
Lean back until you balance just behind the sit bones and lift the chest so the spine stays long.
Lift the shins until they are parallel to the floor, then straighten the legs as far as the back stays flat.
Reach the arms forward beside the legs and hold the position for the prescribed time.
Lower the feet under control to finish.
tips: Keep the chest lifted; the moment the back rounds, bend the knees again.
Hold behind the thighs if the hamstrings limit you more than the core does.
Breathe steadily instead of bracing against a held breath.

bodyweight-overhead-press.description: An unloaded standing overhead press: the arms press up from the shoulders until they are straight overhead, rehearsing the pressing pattern for the shoulders and triceps without any equipment.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands in loose fists at shoulder height, palms facing forward and elbows under the wrists.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your ribs stay down.
Press both arms straight up until the elbows are fully extended and the upper arms are beside your ears.
Lower your hands back to shoulder height under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Finish with your hands directly over your shoulders, not in front of your face.
Do not lean back or arch your lower back to get the arms higher.
Once the pattern feels smooth, hold light dumbbells or a band to add load.

box-jump.description: A plyometric jump from a quarter-squat onto a stable box, training lower-body power.
instructions: Stand a foot in front of a sturdy box with feet shoulder-width.
Drop into a quarter-squat and swing the arms back.
Drive the arms up and explode off the floor onto the box.
Land softly with both feet flat and knees bent.
Step down — do not jump down — and reset.
tips: Always step down — repeated drop-landings stress the Achilles.
Land softly with the whole foot, knees tracking over the toes.
Pick a box height you can clear cleanly without piking the hips.

butterfly-stretch.description: A seated stretch for the inner thighs, pressing the soles of the feet together with the knees dropped out.
instructions: Sit tall and press the soles of your feet together.
Let your knees drop out toward the floor.
Hold your feet and sit up tall.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Gently press the knees down with your elbows for more stretch.
Bring your heels closer to your body to increase intensity.

cable-curl.description: A bicep curl using cable resistance for constant tension.
instructions: Stand facing a low cable pulley with a straight bar or EZ-bar attachment.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows from drifting forward as you curl.
Straighten your arms fully at the bottom of each rep.
Avoid leaning back to help lift the weight.

cable-hammer-curl.description: A cable curl using a rope attachment with a neutral grip to target the brachialis and brachioradialis with constant tension.
instructions: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grip the rope with a neutral (hammer) grip, palms facing each other.
Curl the rope upward toward your shoulders, keeping elbows pinned at your sides.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Keep your elbows stationary throughout the movement.
Pull the rope ends apart slightly at the top to increase contraction.
Avoid swinging the torso.

cable-pallof-press.description: An anti-rotation core exercise in which a cable pulls you sideways while you press a handle straight out from your chest and refuse to let your torso turn.
instructions: Set a cable at chest height and take the handle in both hands, standing side-on to the machine.
Step away until there is real tension on the cable, with your feet about shoulder-width apart and knees softly bent.
Bring the handle to the centre of your chest and brace your trunk and glutes.
Press the handle straight out in front of you until your arms are extended, resisting the pull that wants to rotate you toward the machine.
Hold the extended position for a moment, then bring the handle back to your chest under control.
Complete the desired reps, then turn around and repeat facing the other way.
tips: Nothing should rotate. If your shoulders turn toward the cable as you press, reduce the weight — the point is the rotation that does not happen.
The further you step from the machine, the longer the lever and the harder it gets, so you can change difficulty without touching the weight stack.
Keep your arms level with your chest and your shoulders down; letting the handle drift up turns it into a front raise.

cable-upright-row.description: An upright row performed with a cable for constant tension on the lateral deltoids and traps.
instructions: Stand in front of a cable machine and grip a straight bar or rope at thigh height.
Pull the bar up toward your chin, leading with your elbows.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep elbows higher than your wrists.
Avoid shrugging excessively.

captains-chair-knee-raise.description: A bodyweight core exercise performed on a captain's chair that targets the lower abs and hip flexors.
instructions: Position yourself in the captain's chair with your back flat against the pad and forearms on the armrests.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Engage your core and raise your knees toward your chest.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Avoid swinging the legs for momentum.
Exhale as you raise your knees.
Keep your back pressed against the pad throughout.

chair-pose.description: A standing hold with the hips sunk back and the arms overhead, so the quadriceps and the upper back work isometrically against bodyweight.
instructions: Stand with the feet together or hip-width apart and the weight in the heels.
Bend the knees and send the hips back as if sitting down onto a chair.
Raise the arms overhead beside the ears, keeping the ribs from flaring.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the chest lifted and the knees tracking over the toes.
Press through the heels to stand back up.
tips: Keep enough weight in the heels that you could lift the toes.
Take the arms slightly forward if raising them fully makes the lower back arch.
Sink lower for more quadriceps work, but only while the heels stay down.

chest-supported-dumbbell-shrug.description: A shrug performed face-down on an incline bench, the chest support isolating the traps and removing momentum.
instructions: Set an incline bench to about 30 degrees.
Lie face down on the bench holding dumbbells at arm's length.
Shrug your shoulders up and back toward your ears.
Squeeze your upper traps at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Shrug up and back toward your ears rather than straight up.
Keep your chest pinned to the pad so you cannot use body english.
Pause and squeeze at the top before lowering under control.

childs-pose.description: A kneeling rest stretch that lengthens the lats, lower back and shoulders with the arms reaching forward.
instructions: Kneel and sit your hips back toward your heels.
Fold your torso forward over your thighs.
Reach both arms out long on the floor in front.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Spread your knees wider to rest your chest lower.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

clamshells-hold.description: The top position of the clamshell held for time: lying on one side with the knees bent and stacked, the upper knee lifted and the pelvis square, so the glute medius works isometrically instead of through repetitions.
instructions: Lie on one side with the hips and knees bent about 45 and 90 degrees, heels together and knees stacked.
Stack the shoulders and hips vertically and brace the trunk so the pelvis cannot roll backwards.
Open the upper knee as far as it goes without the pelvis rotating, keeping the heels touching.
Hold that open position for the prescribed time, breathing normally.
Lower the knee under control and repeat on the other side.
tips: Stop the lift where the pelvis starts to roll back; the range is smaller than most people expect.
Keep the heels pressed together so the movement stays in the hip rather than the ankle.
Add a loop band above the knees only once the pelvis stays perfectly still.

close-grip-barbell-curl.description: A standing barbell curl with a narrow grip, biasing the long head of the biceps and the brachialis.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width apart.
Start with the bar at the thighs, arms extended, elbows tucked to the sides.
Curl the bar up to the shoulders by flexing the elbows.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the elbows pinned to the sides — do not let them drift forward.
If the narrow grip bothers your wrists, use an EZ-bar.

close-grip-ez-bar-curl.description: An EZ-bar biceps curl with hands close together, biasing the long head of the biceps.
instructions: Stand holding an EZ-bar with hands on the inner bends, palms up.
Keep the elbows tucked at the sides.
Curl the bar up to shoulder level, squeezing the biceps.
Lower under control to a full stretch.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
tips: Keep the elbows pinned — do not let them flare forward.
Squeeze hard at the top.
Avoid swinging the torso for momentum.

close-grip-push-ups.description: A push-up variation with hands placed close together to emphasize the triceps.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with hands directly under your shoulders.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows tracking backward, not flared out.
Maintain a rigid plank position throughout.
Slow the descent for greater triceps activation.

commando-pull-up.description: A pull-up variation done with a staggered grip: the hands sit one in front of the other on the bar and the body is turned sideways, so the head passes beside the bar on each repetition. It demands more from the lats, arms and trunk than a standard pull-up.
instructions: Grip the bar with the hands one in front of the other, palms facing each other, and hang with the arms straight and the body turned sideways.
Brace the trunk and pull the shoulder blades down to start the movement.
Pull yourself up, driving the elbows down, until your head clears the bar on one side of it.
Pause briefly at the top with the chest close to the bar.
Lower under control to a full hang.
Take the head to the other side of the bar on the next repetition, or swap the hand positions each set.
tips: Keep the legs and trunk still; swinging turns the pull into a kip.
Alternate the sides evenly so both arms and lats do the same work.
Start with a few repetitions per set: the staggered grip is harder than a regular pull-up.

cossack-squat.description: A wide-stance lateral squat that sinks the body deep over one bent leg while the other stays straight, training single-leg strength, hip mobility, and adductor flexibility.
instructions: Stand in a wide stance with toes turned slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side, bending that knee and sinking into a deep squat.
Keep the trailing leg straight with the heel down and toes up.
Sink as low as your mobility allows, keeping the chest tall.
Drive through the bent leg back to center, then repeat to the other side.
tips: Keep the working heel planted -- do not roll onto the toes.
Point the straight leg's toes up to keep tension in the adductors.
Hold a light weight at your chest for a counterbalance if needed.

cross-body-crunch.description: A floor oblique crunch that draws the opposite elbow and knee toward each other, hitting the obliques and rectus together.
instructions: Lie face-up on the floor with knees bent and hands lightly behind the ears.
Crunch up and rotate, bringing the right elbow toward the left knee as the knee draws up.
Return to the starting position under control.
Repeat on the other side, alternating every rep.
tips: Twist from the ribcage, not the arms; the elbows follow the shoulders.
Lower back stays on the floor throughout.

crunches.description: A basic abdominal exercise focusing on the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and hands behind your head.
Curl your upper body toward your knees, lifting your shoulder blades off the floor.
Squeeze your abs at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.
Exhale as you curl up and inhale on the way down.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.

db-fly.description: An isolation exercise that stretches and contracts the pectorals through a wide arc of motion.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with dumbbells held above your chest, palms facing each other.
With a slight bend in the elbows, lower the dumbbells out to the sides.
Return to the start by squeezing your chest.
Repeat.
tips: Keep a consistent bend in the elbows throughout.
Do not let the dumbbells go too low.

db-overhead-carry.description: A loaded walk with a single dumbbell locked out overhead, demanding shoulder stability and an upright trunk over every step.
instructions: Clean or press a dumbbell to a locked-out position directly above your shoulder.
Push the arm all the way up so the elbow is straight and the biceps is close to your ear.
Brace your ribs down rather than letting your lower back arch to hold the weight up.
Walk forward with controlled strides, keeping the dumbbell stacked over your shoulder and hip.
Keep your eyes forward — tipping your head back to watch the weight drags your posture with it.
Carry for the desired distance, lower under control, then repeat with the other arm.
tips: Match the distance on both arms so the asymmetric load does not become an asymmetric adaptation.
A locked elbow is not optional. A soft elbow puts the whole load on the muscle instead of the skeleton and the set ends early.
If your ribs flare and your back arches, the weight is too heavy for your current overhead position — fix the position before adding load.

db-reverse-wrist-curl.description: A dumbbell wrist curl with palms down, training the forearm extensors.
instructions: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, forearms resting on your thighs, palms down.
Let both wrists drop, lowering the dumbbells toward the floor.
Lift the backs of your hands toward the ceiling by extending your wrists.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Use a much lighter load than for a regular wrist curl.
Move only at the wrist.
Squeeze the back of the forearm at the top.

db-squat.description: A squat loaded with a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, accessible without a barbell.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width, a dumbbell in each hand at the sides.
Brace the core and keep the chest up.
Squat down by hinging at the hips and bending the knees.
Descend until the thighs are parallel or below.
Drive through the heels to stand back up.
tips: Keep the chest up and the back flat throughout.
Push the knees out in line with the toes.
Use straps if grip becomes the limiting factor.

dead-bug.description: A supine core exercise coordinating opposite limb extension to train deep core stability.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms extended toward the ceiling and knees at 90 degrees.
Lower your right arm and left leg toward the floor while keeping the lower back pressed down.
Return to start.
Repeat on the other side.
Alternate.
tips: Press your lower back into the floor at all times.
Move slowly.

decline-bench-press.description: A compound chest press on a decline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, targeting the lower pectorals.
instructions: Set the bench to a decline angle. Lie down and secure your feet.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, then lower them to the sides of your lower chest.
Press the dumbbells back up to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your back flat on the bench.
Use a spotter when working with heavier loads.

decline-db-fly.description: An isolation fly movement performed on a decline bench to emphasize the lower chest.
instructions: Lie on a decline bench holding dumbbells above your chest.
With a slight elbow bend, lower the dumbbells wide to each side.
Squeeze the chest to bring them back up.
Repeat.
tips: Do not fully lock out the elbows.
Focus on the stretch at the bottom.

deficit-push-ups.description: A push-up variation with hands on raised supports, lowering the chest below hand level for a greater range of motion.
instructions: Place your hands on two elevated surfaces like parallettes or blocks.
Assume a plank position with hands under your shoulders.
Lower your chest below the level of your hands.
Press back up to extend your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Avoid letting your hips sag during the deep stretch.
Work within a pain-free depth and increase it gradually.
Keep your elbows tracking back rather than flaring wide.

donkey-calf-raise.description: A bent-over calf raise that maximizes calf stretch by hinging at the hips.
instructions: Bend at the hips and place your hands on the floor in front of you, hips high and legs nearly straight.
Set your feet hip-width apart with your weight on the balls of the feet.
Lower your heels as far as they go (below the edge if you stand on a raised platform) for a full stretch.
Drive up onto the toes as high as possible, squeezing the calves.
Lower under control to a deep stretch.
tips: Pause briefly at the top to maximize the contraction.
Use a slow eccentric for full stretch.
Add a partner or weight on the lower back for resistance.

double-kettlebell-bicep-curl.description: A standing biceps curl with one kettlebell in each hand, held by the handle. The offset mass at the bottom of the bell adds a mild grip and stability challenge.
instructions: Stand holding a kettlebell in each hand by the handle, palms facing forward.
Keep the elbows tucked to the sides and the bells hanging at arm length.
Curl both kettlebells up toward the shoulders by flexing the elbows.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Do not let the bells swing — control the eccentric.
Elbows stay pinned to the sides; no shoulder flexion.
Grip hard throughout; the bell wants to pull the wrist into extension.

double-kettlebell-dead-split-snatch.description: An Olympic-style kettlebell lift snatching two bells from the floor to overhead, caught in a split stance.
instructions: Set two kettlebells on the floor between your feet.
Hinge down and grip both handles firmly.
Explosively pull the kettlebells overhead in one motion.
Drop into a split stance to catch them at lockout.
Recover by stepping feet back together.
tips: Punch up through the handles to achieve a stable overhead lockout.
Keep your front knee tracking over your foot in the split.
Stay tall through your torso as you drop under the bells.

double-kettlebell-push-press.description: A push press with two kettlebells in the rack. The leg drive (single dip) lets you launch heavier loads overhead than a strict press — the middle tier between strict OHP and full jerk.
instructions: Stand with two kettlebells racked at the shoulders, elbows down and tucked.
Feet shoulder-width, core braced.
Dip the knees slightly while keeping the torso vertical.
Explosively extend the legs and press both bells overhead in one motion.
Lock out with the bells over the mid-foot.
Lower back to the rack under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Only ONE dip — if you re-bend the knees under the bell, that is a jerk.
Drive from the legs, the arms finish.
The torso stays vertical throughout; no lean.

double-kettlebell-swing-snatch.description: A ballistic kettlebell exercise swinging two bells from between the legs to an overhead lockout in one motion.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding two kettlebells.
Hinge at the hips to swing the bells between your legs.
Explosively drive your hips forward to swing the bells up.
Punch through to catch both kettlebells overhead with locked arms.
Lower under control and repeat.
tips: Keep your arms relaxed and let your hips generate the power.
Let the bells roll smoothly around your wrists rather than flipping over.
Maintain a flat back during every backswing.

downward-dog-to-knee-drive.description: From three-legged dog the lifted leg folds forward so the knee travels towards the elbow or the nose, then extends back up. The shoulders hold the position while the trunk does the folding, one side at a time.
instructions: Set up in downward dog and lift one leg behind you into three-legged dog.
Press both hands down and shift the weight slightly forward.
Round the upper back and drive that knee forward towards the elbow or the nose.
Extend the leg back up to three-legged dog under control.
Finish the repetitions on that side and repeat on the other.
tips: Let the upper back round as the knee comes in; a flat back stops the knee short.
Keep the shoulders over the wrists as you shift forward rather than collapsing past them.
Lift the leg only as high as the hips stay level on the way back out.

drag-curl.description: A barbell curl where the elbows travel backward and the bar drags up the torso, eliminating front-delt assistance and emphasizing the long head of the biceps.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Start with the bar at the thighs and elbows at the sides.
Curl the bar by sliding (dragging) it straight up along your body.
As the bar rises, let the elbows travel backward so the bar stays in contact with your torso.
Stop when the bar reaches mid-chest; the biceps will be fully shortened.
Lower under control along the same path and repeat.
tips: Use significantly less weight than a standard curl — the altered mechanics make it much harder.
The bar should never move away from the body.

dumbbell-clean-and-press.description: A full-body power exercise in which two dumbbells are cleaned to the shoulders and then pressed overhead in one flowing sequence. It builds explosive hip power and strong shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand, hanging at your sides.
Hinge at the hips and bend the knees slightly to lower the dumbbells to just below the knees.
Explosively extend the hips and knees and shrug to pull the dumbbells up to the shoulders, catching them with the elbows forward.
Dip slightly at the knees and drive the dumbbells straight overhead until the arms are locked out.
Lower the dumbbells back to the shoulders, then to your sides, under control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Let the legs and hips produce the power; the arms only guide the dumbbells.
Keep the dumbbells close to the body on the way up.
Finish each press with the ribs down and the glutes tight.

dumbbell-farmers-walk.description: This full-body exercise involves walking while holding heavy dumbbells, effectively building grip strength, core stability, and overall muscular endurance.
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended at your sides.
Retract your shoulder blades and brace your core, maintaining a neutral spine.
Walk slowly and deliberately for a set distance or duration, taking short, controlled steps.
Keep your chest up and avoid leaning to one side as you walk.
Focus on maintaining a strong, stable posture throughout the movement.
tips: Use the heaviest dumbbells you can control without compromising form.
Breathe deeply and rhythmically to maintain core tension.
Imagine you are balancing a glass of water on your head.

dumbbell-hip-thrust.description: The Dumbbell Hip Thrust is a highly effective compound exercise for building strong glutes and hamstrings, performed by thrusting the hips upwards with a dumbbell across the pelvis.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, knees bent, feet flat, and a dumbbell across your hips.
Brace your core and drive through your heels, lifting your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes powerfully at the top of the movement, ensuring full hip extension.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position with control, maintaining tension.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chin tucked towards your chest to maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Focus on driving through your heels to maximize glute activation.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to enhance muscle growth.
Use a pad or towel under the dumbbell for comfort.

dumbbell-romanian-deadlift.description: A hip-hinge movement with dumbbells and soft knees, loading the hamstrings and glutes through a controlled stretch.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs with a soft knee bend.
Hinge at the hips and push your glutes back.
Lower the dumbbells along your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Keep your back flat and shoulders pulled back.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your knee angle constant; the movement is a hinge, not a squat.
Tuck your chin slightly to keep your spine in one straight line.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without leaning backward.

dumbbell-split-squat.description: A split-stance squat holding dumbbells at the sides, training the quads and glutes one leg at a time.
instructions: Stand in a split stance holding dumbbells at your sides.
Keep your torso upright and core braced.
Lower your back knee toward the floor by bending both knees.
Stop when your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep most of your weight on your front leg.
Lower your back knee straight down toward the floor.
Track your front knee over your toes without letting it cave inward.

dumbbell-wrist-curl.description: A dumbbell wrist curl that isolates the forearm flexors and trains both arms independently.
instructions: Sit on a bench with the forearm resting on the thigh, palm up.
Hold a dumbbell with the wrist hanging off the knee.
Let the dumbbell roll down to the fingertips.
Curl the dumbbell up by flexing the wrist.
Lower under control. Complete reps per side.
tips: Move only at the wrist — keep the forearm still.
Roll the dumbbell to the fingertips for full range.
Train both arms with the same load and reps.

extended-side-angle.description: A wide-stance standing pose with the front knee bent and the torso extended over the front thigh, so one long line runs from the back heel to the top hand.
instructions: Stand wide with the front foot turned out and the back foot angled slightly in.
Bend the front knee until it stacks over the ankle and keep the back leg straight.
Rest the front forearm on the thigh, or the hand on the floor or a block, and reach the top arm over the ear.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, turning the chest towards the ceiling.
Straighten the front leg to come up and repeat on the other side.
tips: Press the outer edge of the back foot down; the pose loses its base as soon as that heel lifts.
Keep the front knee pointing at the middle toes rather than drifting inwards.
Take the forearm on the thigh instead of the hand on the floor to keep the chest open.

ez-bar-lying-tricep-extension.description: A lying triceps extension performed with an EZ bar to isolate the triceps through a full range of motion.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar over your chest with a narrow grip.
Lower the bar toward your forehead by bending at the elbows.
Extend your arms back to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your upper arms vertical throughout so the triceps do the work.
The EZ bar's angled grip is easier on the wrists than a straight bar.
Lower slowly to protect the elbows.

ez-bar-reverse-grip-row.description: This compound pulling exercise targets the latissimus dorsi and biceps, effectively building back thickness and arm strength with an underhand grip.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Hinge at your hips, keeping a slight bend in your knees and your back straight, until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Let the bar hang directly below your shoulders with arms fully extended.
Pull the bar towards your lower abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together and driving your elbows up.
Control the eccentric phase, slowly lowering the bar back to the starting position with full arm extension.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement to protect your lower back.
Focus on initiating the pull with your lats, not just your biceps.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders; keep them depressed and retracted.
Use a full range of motion, extending your arms completely at the bottom.

ez-bar-upright-row.description: An upright row variation using an EZ-bar for more comfortable wrist positioning.
instructions: Stand holding an EZ-bar with a shoulder-width grip on the angled portions.
Pull the bar straight up along your body toward your chin.
Lead with your elbows, keeping them above your hands.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Pull only as high as your shoulders allow without pinching.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout the movement.
Avoid swinging or using your legs to lift the weight.

fish-pose.description: A supine backbend supported on the forearms with the chest lifted and the head tilted back, opening the front of the chest and the throat.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs straight and the arms alongside the body, palms down under the hips.
Press the forearms into the floor and lift the chest towards the ceiling.
Let the crown of the head rest lightly on the floor without putting weight through the neck.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, breathing into the upper chest.
Lift the head, then lower the back down.
tips: Carry the weight in the forearms, not the head; the neck only guides the position.
Place a block lengthwise under the upper back if the floor version pinches.
Keep the legs active and the thighs rolling slightly inwards.

floor-press.description: A barbell pressing movement performed on the floor, limiting range of motion and taking the lower body out of the equation.
instructions: Lie on the floor and position yourself under a barbell in a rack.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your chest until your upper arms touch the floor.
Press back up to lockout.
Repeat.
tips: Elbows touching the floor provides a natural stopping point.
Useful for addressing lockout weakness.

front-squat.description: A barbell squat with the bar held in front on the deltoids, emphasizing quads and core.
instructions: Clean or rack the bar to your front deltoids with elbows high.
Squat down keeping torso upright until thighs are parallel.
Drive back up.
Repeat.
tips: Maintain high elbows to keep the bar stable.
A more upright torso increases quad activation.

glute-kickback.description: A bodyweight glute isolation exercise performed on all fours to develop gluteus maximus strength and shape.
instructions: Begin on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, drive one heel toward the ceiling.
Squeeze the glute at the top of the movement.
Lower the leg back to the starting position with control.
Complete all reps, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips square to the floor — avoid rotating.
Focus on squeezing the glute, not just lifting the leg.
Add a resistance band or cable for progressive overload.

hack-squat.description: A compound lower-body machine exercise on the hack squat sled, targeting the quadriceps through a guided squat pattern.
instructions: Load the hack squat machine and step on, positioning your back and shoulders against the pads.
Place your feet shoulder-width on the platform with toes turned out slightly.
Unlock the safety handles and lower the sled by bending at the knees and hips.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Drive through your heels to extend the legs and push the sled back to the start.
Re-engage the safety handles after your final rep.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed against the pad throughout the movement.
Placing the feet higher on the platform shifts emphasis to the glutes and hamstrings.
Control the descent; do not bounce out of the bottom position.

hammer-curl.description: A bicep curl variation with a neutral grip targeting the brachioradialis.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing each other.
Curl the weights up while keeping your palms facing inward.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides throughout.
Keep your wrists straight and rigid throughout the curl.
Avoid leaning back or swinging the weights up.

hang-power-clean.description: A clean from the hang caught in a partial squat, building explosive power without dropping into a full squat.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a barbell at your thighs.
Hinge at the hips to lower the bar to just above the knees.
Drive through your hips and legs explosively.
Pull the bar up and catch it on your front shoulders in a partial squat.
Stand tall with the bar racked on your shoulders.
Lower the bar back to the hang position.
tips: Drive through your hips and legs before the arms pull.
Receive the bar with your thighs above parallel.
Keep your back flat as you hinge to the start position.

hanging-leg-raise.description: An advanced core exercise performed hanging from a bar.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip.
Raise your legs in front of you until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
Avoid swinging.
Repeat.
tips: Curl your pelvis up at the top to fully engage your abs.
Keep your shoulders engaged rather than hanging passively.
Bend your knees to make the movement easier if needed.

head-to-knee-pose.description: A seated one-legged fold: one leg stays straight while the other foot rests against the inner thigh, so the hamstring of the straight leg lengthens one side at a time.
instructions: Sit with one leg straight in front of you and the other knee bent out to the side, that foot at the inner thigh.
Turn the chest towards the straight leg so the navel lines up with the thigh.
Hinge from the hips and reach forward along the straight leg with a long spine.
Hold the fold for the prescribed time, breathing into the back of the leg.
Come up with a flat back and repeat on the other side.
tips: Sit on a folded blanket so the pelvis can tip forward instead of the back rounding.
Keep the toes of the straight leg pointing up rather than rolling out.
Use a strap around the foot when the hands do not reach it comfortably.

heel-touches.description: A lying core exercise in which you crunch slightly to one side and reach the hand toward the heel, then alternate sides. It trains the obliques and the upper abdominals with the lower back kept on the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Lift the head and shoulders slightly off the floor and reach the arms down along your sides.
Crunch to one side and reach that hand toward the heel on the same side.
Return to the center and reach toward the opposite heel.
Keep alternating sides in a smooth rhythm while the lower back stays on the floor.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the neck long and the chin off the chest; lead with the ribcage, not the head.
Keep each reach small and controlled; the shoulder blades only just clear the floor.
Keep the feet planted and the lower back pressed into the floor throughout.

high-knees.description: A bodyweight cardio drill where the knees are driven up to hip height in rapid alternation.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up toward the chest while pumping the opposite arm.
Quickly switch legs, mirroring the arm action.
Continue alternating at a fast pace.
Continue for the prescribed work interval.
tips: Drive the knees up to at least hip height.
Stay light on the balls of the feet.
Keep the torso upright — do not lean back.

hip-thrust.description: A compound glute exercise using a barbell across the hips.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, barbell across your hips.
Drive your hips up until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower your hips back down with control.
Repeat.
tips: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down at the top.
Finish with your shins vertical, driving through your heels.
Reach full hip extension without arching your lower back.

hyperextension-hold-bench.description: An isometric hold on a hyperextension bench: you lift your torso until your body forms one straight line from the heels to the head and hold it there. The erector spinae and the glutes stay under tension without the swinging of the dynamic back extension.
instructions: Adjust the bench so that the pad sits just below your hip bones and your heels are hooked firmly behind the roller or pad.
Cross your arms over your chest and lower your torso toward the floor with a straight back.
Raise your torso until your body is in one straight line from your head to your heels.
Stop in that line and hold, with your glutes squeezed and your neck in line with your spine.
Keep your breathing slow and do not arch your lower back past the straight line while you hold for the planned time.
Lower your torso under control and rest.
tips: Stop at a straight line; leaning back past it hands the work to your lower back joints instead of the muscles.
Squeeze the glutes during the whole hold, so that the hips stay extended and the lower back is not doing the job alone.
Hold a weight plate against your chest only after you can hold bodyweight for a full minute.

incline-db-curl.description: A bicep curl on an incline bench for a deeper stretch of the long head.
instructions: Sit on an incline bench set to 45 degrees, holding dumbbells at your sides.
Let your arms hang straight down with palms forward.
Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Lower with control to full extension.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders against the bench throughout.
Don't let your elbows drift forward as you curl.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders forward as you lift the weight.

incline-plank-hold.description: An easier version of the plank: with your forearms resting on a flat bench and your feet on the floor, you hold your body in a straight line from head to heels. The raised hands reduce the load on the shoulders and make it a good starting point for the full plank.
instructions: Place your forearms on a flat bench, with your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Step your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and pull your belly button toward your spine to keep your hips level.
Keep your neck long and look at a point on the bench slightly ahead of your hands.
Hold the position for the planned time while breathing steadily.
Step your feet in to finish.
tips: Do not let your hips sag toward the bench or pike up; your body should stay in one straight line.
Press your forearms into the bench and push the bench away to keep your shoulder blades wide.
Step your feet further back to make it harder, or closer to make it easier; make sure the bench cannot slide.

isometric-neck-side.description: A static side-neck drill using the hand as resistance against the head, training the sternocleidomastoid and scalene without hardware.
instructions: Sit or stand tall. Place the palm of one hand against the side of the head, above the ear.
Press the head into the hand while resisting equally with the hand — the head does not move.
Hold the isometric contraction for 5 to 10 seconds.
Release slowly, then repeat on the same side for the set.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Match the pressure; this is 50% effort, not a wrestling match.
Keep the jaw relaxed and the shoulders down.

jump-rope.description: A classic cardio drill that trains calves, ankles, and timing with a rope and rhythmic hops.
instructions: Hold a jump rope handle in each hand with the rope behind you.
Swing the rope overhead and forward in a smooth arc.
Hop just high enough for the rope to pass under your feet.
Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees slightly bent.
Keep a steady rhythm for the prescribed interval.
tips: Use the wrists to spin the rope, not the shoulders.
Hop low — only an inch or two off the floor.
Stay tall with elbows close to the sides.

kettlebell-bottoms-up-hold.description: A one-arm hold in which the kettlebell is held upside down by the handle at shoulder height, with the bell above your hand. Keeping the bell level demands a very firm grip and constant work from the forearm and the shoulder, which makes this a strong test of wrist and shoulder stability.
instructions: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder and flip it so that the bell points up and the handle sits in your fist.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your free arm relaxed at your side.
Keep your forearm vertical and your elbow close to your ribs, with the bell directly above your hand.
Grip the handle firmly and keep your wrist straight, as if you were balancing a cup.
Hold the bell steady for the planned time, breathing slowly and keeping your shoulder down.
Lower the kettlebell with control, turn it the right way up and switch arms.
tips: Start with a very light bell; a weight that feels easy when held the normal way can be hard to keep level.
Keep the shoulder down and the wrist stacked over the forearm; if the bell tips, reset the position before it falls.
Stand in a clear space, away from people and furniture, in case the bell tips.

kettlebell-curl.description: A biceps curl with one kettlebell held by the handle in both hands. The kettlebell hangs in front of your thighs and you curl it up toward your chest, keeping the elbows close to your sides; sharing the load between two hands makes it an easy way to start training the biceps.
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold the kettlebell by its handle with both hands, so it hangs in front of your thighs.
Keep your elbows close to your sides, your chest tall and your shoulders relaxed.
Bend your elbows and curl the kettlebell up toward your chest without letting your upper arms swing forward.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, with the kettlebell close to your chest.
Lower the kettlebell slowly until your arms are straight again, keeping control of the swing of the bell.
Repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Hold the handle firmly with both hands and keep your wrists straight, so the kettlebell does not roll or tilt.
Do not lean back or swing your hips to lift the kettlebell; if you have to, the weight is too heavy.
Take about twice as long to lower the kettlebell as to lift it, so the biceps work through the whole descent.

kettlebell-floor-press.description: A two-arm chest press performed lying on the floor with a kettlebell in each hand. The floor caps the ROM (triceps hit the floor before full stretch), making it shoulder-friendly and a great home option.
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent, feet flat.
Hold a kettlebell in each hand at the chest, bells resting on the outer forearms.
Press both kettlebells straight up until the arms are fully extended.
Lower under control until the triceps touch the floor — do not bounce.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Elbows stay about 45 degrees from the torso; do not flare.
The grip matters: keep the bells stable against the outside of the forearms.
The floor limits ROM by design — this is the feature, not the bug.

kettlebell-hip-thrust.description: This exercise effectively targets the gluteus maximus and hamstrings, using a kettlebell to add resistance for powerful hip extension and glute development.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat.
Place a kettlebell across your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Drive through your heels, lifting your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes forcefully at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your chin tucked towards your chest to maintain a neutral spine.
Focus on pushing through your heels to maximize glute activation.
Ensure your knees track in line with your toes throughout the movement.
Control the eccentric phase, resisting the weight as you lower your hips.

kettlebell-overhead-carry.description: A loaded walk with a single kettlebell locked out overhead, where the bell hangs behind the wrist and pulls the arm backwards, making it harder to hold still than a dumbbell.
instructions: Clean and press a kettlebell to lockout, letting the bell settle on the back of your forearm.
Straighten the elbow fully and turn the arm so the bell sits behind and above your wrist rather than off to the side.
Keep the shoulder active: push the weight up toward the ceiling and let the shoulder blade rotate up with it rather than forcing it down.
Brace your trunk and walk forward with even strides, keeping the bell stacked over your shoulder and hip.
Keep your wrist straight; letting it bend back is what makes an overhead bell feel unstable.
Carry for the desired distance, lower under control, then repeat on the other side.
tips: Go lighter than you would with a dumbbell. The offset mass makes the same weight noticeably harder to keep still.
A bent wrist is the usual failure point. If it keeps collapsing, drop the weight rather than fighting it for the whole distance.
Do both sides for the same distance — the unilateral load is the point of the exercise.

kettlebell-pullover.description: A pullover on a flat bench with a kettlebell held by the horns. The deep overhead stretch hits the lats, long-head triceps, and serratus.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands above the chest, arms nearly straight (slight elbow bend).
Keeping the elbow angle fixed, lower the bell overhead in an arc until the upper arms are in line with the torso.
Pull the bell back above the chest along the same arc.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the lower back pressed into the bench — do not arch to steal ROM.
Grip the horns hard; the bell will try to flip over at the bottom.
Go only as deep as your shoulder mobility allows without pain.

kettlebell-rotational-lunge.description: A reverse lunge holding a kettlebell at the chest, adding a torso rotation toward the front leg to work the legs and obliques together.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell with both hands at your chest.
Step back into a lunge, lowering until both knees are bent.
Rotate your torso toward the front leg.
Move the kettlebell to that side at chest to shoulder height, arms almost straight.
Rotate back to the center and push through the front foot to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep the front knee over the ankle as you lower into the lunge.
Rotate from your torso and hips, not your knees.
Keep your chest tall as you rotate.

kettlebell-skull-crusher.description: A skull crusher lying on the floor, holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands. The offset mass hangs below the wrists, adding a grip and control challenge.
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands, arms extended above the chest.
Bend the elbows to lower the bell in a controlled arc past your forehead to behind your head, until it nearly touches the floor.
Keep the upper arms still, angled slightly back toward your head; only the forearms move.
Extend the elbows to press the bell back up.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Grip the horns firmly — the bell tries to rotate forward at the bottom.
Elbows stay narrow — if they flare, the load is too heavy.
Angle the upper arms slightly back toward the head to keep tension on the triceps at lockout.

kettlebell-svend-press.description: A standing chest exercise pressing one kettlebell forward from the chest, held by the handle with both hands; squeezing the hands together on the handle keeps the pecs under tension.
instructions: Stand holding one kettlebell by the handle with both hands at chest height, the bell hanging below your hands.
Squeeze your hands together on the handle to tense the chest.
Press the kettlebell forward until your arms are almost straight.
Pull it back to the chest under control.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
tips: Keep pushing the hands toward each other on the handle throughout; without that squeeze it turns into a front-shoulder raise.
Use a light kettlebell — the long lever of straight arms dictates the load.
Keep the elbows slightly bent at the lockout.

kettlebell-turkish-get-ups.description: A full-body kettlebell exercise that moves from lying to standing while holding the weight locked out overhead, training total-body strength, stability, and mobility.
instructions: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell pressed overhead in one hand.
Bend the knee on the same side and plant the foot flat.
Roll up onto your opposite elbow, then to your hand.
Drive your hips up and sweep your straight leg back into a lunge.
Stand up fully while keeping the kettlebell locked out overhead.
Reverse the sequence to return to the start.
tips: Keep your eyes on the kettlebell until you are standing, then look forward.
Move slowly through each step — the get-up is a sequence, not one motion.

knee-to-chest-stretch.description: A lying stretch that releases the glutes and lower back by hugging one knee into the chest.
instructions: Lie on your back with both legs straight.
Pull one knee in and hug it to your chest with both hands.
Keep the other leg relaxed on the floor.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Relax and keep breathing throughout.

l-sit.description: An advanced static hold with legs extended parallel to the floor, demanding hip flexor and core strength.
instructions: Sit on the floor or press up on parallel bars with arms straight.
Lock your elbows and depress your shoulders.
Lift your legs straight out in front of you parallel to the floor.
Form an L shape with your body.
Hold the position for the prescribed duration.
Lower your legs with control to exit.
tips: Bend your knees into a tuck position if the full hold is too hard.
Point your toes and squeeze your quads to keep legs straight.
Breathe steadily during the hold rather than holding your breath.

lateral-leg-swing.description: A dynamic hip-mobility drill in which one leg swings across the body and out to the side while the standing leg and trunk remain controlled.
instructions: Stand tall and brace the trunk, using a stable support if needed.
Shift the weight onto one leg and lift the other foot slightly from the floor.
Swing the free leg across the front of the body.
Reverse the motion and swing it out to the side through a comfortable range.
Continue smoothly, then change legs.
tips: Keep the pelvis facing forward instead of rotating with the swinging leg.
Use a range you can control without leaning the torso.
Let the movement grow gradually rather than forcing the first repetition.

leg-extension.description: An isolation exercise for the quadriceps using a machine.
instructions: Sit in the leg extension machine with ankles behind the pad.
Extend your legs until they are straight.
Squeeze your quads at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Adjust the seat so your knees align with the machine's pivot point.
Keep your back pressed against the pad throughout.
Avoid swinging the weight up with momentum.

lizard-stretch.description: A deep lunge stretch that opens the hip flexors, groin and glutes with the forearms lowered toward the floor.
instructions: Step one foot forward into a deep lunge, foot placed wide.
Lower both forearms toward the floor inside the front foot.
Extend the back leg straight and let the hips sink.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Rest on your hands instead of forearms for an easier version.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.

lunge.description: A bodyweight forward lunge stepping into a long stride, training the quads, glutes, and balance one leg at a time.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step forward with one leg into a long stride.
Lower your back knee toward the floor until both knees form 90-degree angles.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Take a stride long enough for both knees to reach about 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright and eyes forward.
Push through the front heel to return in one strong motion.

machine-back-extension.description: A seated machine isolation exercise for the lower back: with the hips and legs held in place, the torso is driven backwards against a padded lever to extend the spine against a weight stack.
instructions: Sit in the back extension machine with your feet flat on the foot platform and the roller pad set behind your upper back, just below the shoulder blades.
Grip the handles at your sides and let your torso come forward into a slight flexion — this is the starting position.
Push back against the pad by extending your spine until your torso is leaning back and your lower back is fully contracted.
Pause briefly at full extension, then return to the starting position under control, resisting the weight stack on the way back.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Set the pad across your upper back just below the shoulder blades — too high and it presses on your neck, too low and you lose range of motion.
Extend with your lower back rather than throwing your head and shoulders backwards, and keep both directions slow.
Stop at a neutral, fully extended trunk instead of forcing the spine past it, and start light — the lower back responds better to controlled reps than to heavy loads.

machine-preacher-curl.description: A preacher curl performed on a plate-loaded or selectorized machine, locking the elbows on a pad and providing a fixed strength curve.
instructions: Sit at a preacher curl machine and adjust the seat so your armpits sit at the top of the pad.
Place the upper arms flat on the pad and grip the handles.
Start with the arms extended — but not locked — at the bottom.
Curl the handles up by flexing the elbows; squeeze hard at the top.
Lower slowly back to the starting position and repeat.
tips: Do not let the elbows lift off the pad at the top.
Stop just short of full extension at the bottom to protect the elbow tendons.

machine-triceps-extension.description: A seated machine isolation exercise in which the upper arms stay supported on a pad while the elbows extend against two handles, loading the triceps along a fixed path without help from the shoulders or torso.
instructions: Sit in the tricep extension machine with your back against the seat pad and your upper arms resting flat on the arm pad in front of your chest.
Take a handle in each hand with your elbows bent and your hands up near shoulder height.
Keeping your upper arms pressed into the pad, extend your elbows to drive the handles down and away until your arms are straight.
Squeeze your triceps at full extension, then bend your elbows to return to the start under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Set the seat height so your upper arms lie flat on the pad and your elbows line up with the machine's pivot — that alignment is what keeps the work on the triceps.
Keep your upper arms glued to the pad; letting them lift turns the movement into a press and takes the triceps out of it.
Straighten your arms fully without snapping the elbows, and resist on the way back instead of letting the weight stack drop.

mountain-pose.description: The basic standing posture: feet grounded, legs active, spine tall and shoulders relaxed. It is the reference alignment every other standing pose is measured against.
instructions: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and spread the weight evenly across both feet.
Engage the thighs lightly and let the tailbone drop so the pelvis is neutral.
Stack the ribs over the pelvis and the head over the ribs, arms relaxed by the sides.
Hold the posture for the prescribed time, breathing evenly.
Notice where the weight sits and rebalance it towards the middle of each foot.
tips: Lift and spread the toes once, then set them down; it resets the arch of the foot.
Keep the knees soft rather than locked back.
Let the shoulders roll back and down without pinning the shoulder blades together.

negative-pull-ups.description: A pull-up regression emphasizing the slow lowering phase, building back and grip strength toward a full pull-up.
instructions: Use a box or jump to position yourself at the top of a pull-up.
Grip the bar with hands shoulder-width apart.
Hold your chin above the bar briefly.
Lower yourself slowly over 3-5 seconds with control.
Fully extend your arms at the bottom.
Reset and repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Fight for control during the final third of the descent.
Keep your shoulder blades engaged instead of hanging passively.
Stop the set once you can no longer lower slowly.

one-arm-dumbbell-preacher-curl.description: A unilateral biceps curl performed seated at a preacher bench with the upper arm supported on the pad. Training one arm at a time keeps the elbow fixed and isolates the biceps.
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench and rest the back of one upper arm flat on the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in that hand with the palm facing up and the arm almost fully extended.
Curl the dumbbell toward the shoulder without lifting the elbow off the pad.
Squeeze the biceps at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell slowly until the arm is almost straight.
Complete the repetitions, then switch arms.
tips: Stop just short of lockout at the bottom to keep tension on the biceps and spare the elbow.
Keep the shoulder relaxed and the chest against the pad.
Lower the weight more slowly than you lift it.

one-arm-kettlebell-bicep-curl.description: A unilateral kettlebell exercise isolating the biceps, with the offset load adding forearm and grip demand.
instructions: Stand tall holding a kettlebell in one hand.
Keep your elbow pinned to your side.
Curl the kettlebell toward your shoulder by flexing your bicep.
Squeeze at the top of the movement.
Lower the kettlebell with control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep your wrist straight as the offset weight shifts through the curl.
Brace your core to resist leaning away from the working side.
Avoid swinging the kettlebell up with your hips.

one-arm-kettlebell-front-squat.description: A unilateral front squat with one kettlebell racked at the shoulder, challenging the legs and core against the offset load.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in the racked position at one shoulder.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips.
Keep your chest up and torso upright throughout.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep the rack position tight against your chest and forearm.
Resist twisting or leaning toward the loaded side.
Spread the floor with your feet to keep your knees tracking outward.

one-arm-kettlebell-swing.description: A single-arm variation of the kettlebell swing, adding grip and anti-rotation demands to the explosive hip hinge.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a kettlebell on the floor in front of you.
Hinge at the hips and grip the kettlebell with one hand.
Hike the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to swing the kettlebell to chest height.
Let gravity bring the kettlebell back between your legs.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep your shoulders square as the offset load tries to rotate you.
Power the movement with your hips, not by lifting with your arm.
Hinge with a flat back rather than squatting the swing.

one-arm-seated-cable-row.description: A unilateral seated cable row that trains the lats and upper back while the torso stays square and the working shoulder blade moves through a controlled reach and pull.
instructions: Sit at the cable row station and hold one handle with the working arm extended.
Plant the feet, sit tall and brace the trunk without leaning back.
Pull the handle towards the lower ribs while drawing the shoulder blade back.
Pause briefly without rotating the torso or shrugging the shoulder.
Extend the arm under control, finish the set and repeat on the other side.
tips: Keep both shoulders facing forward throughout the repetition.
Drive the elbow back close to the body rather than curling the handle.
Let the shoulder blade reach forward at the start without rounding the lower back.

overhead-tricep-extension.description: An isolation exercise for the triceps emphasizing the long head.
instructions: Stand or sit holding a dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms back to the starting position.
Keep your elbows close to your head throughout.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back.
Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your triceps.
Check your grip is secure before lowering the dumbbell behind your head.

pause-squat.description: A barbell squat variation with a deliberate pause at the bottom, eliminating the stretch reflex to build strength from a dead stop.
instructions: Unrack a barbell and rest it across your upper back.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Hold the bottom position for 2-3 seconds.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Stay braced and tight during the pause rather than relaxing.
Avoid collapsing forward or rocking as you hold the bottom.
Use lighter loads than your regular squat to maintain crisp form.

pec-deck.description: A chest isolation machine with swinging handles that targets the pectorals through horizontal adduction.
instructions: Sit in the pec deck machine and grip the handles with your arms out to the sides, elbows slightly bent.
Adjust the seat so the handles align with mid-chest height.
Squeeze the handles together in front of your chest.
Hold the contraction briefly at the center.
Return under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your shoulders down and back against the seat.
Avoid letting the handles fly back past a comfortable stretch.
Focus on squeezing your chest rather than pressing with your arms.

pilates-kneeling-side-kick.description: A Pilates mat exercise: kneeling on one knee with one hand on the floor for support and the other on the hip, the top leg lifts out to the side up to hip height and lowers again while the trunk holds still.
instructions: Kneel on one knee and place the same-side hand on the floor under the shoulder, the other hand on the hip.
